course.title: Web Security — Complete Deep Security Course
course.description: A defensive, Web Security-specific course progressing from fundamentals to production security, with detailed explanations, safe practicals, dedicated tasks, security testing and a complete learning-platform capstone.
course.curriculumPolicy: Module and lesson counts are determined by the security concepts required to learn the discipline properly; no fixed cross-security template is imposed.
learningOutcomes: Identify assets, threats and trust boundaries.
Secure authentication, authorization and data flows.
Integrate security into development and operations.
Respond to and learn from security failures.

modules.title: Web Security Foundations
modules.description: Browser/server trust boundaries, HTTP, cookies, sessions, origins and attack surfaces.

lessons.title: Web Security Foundations
lessons.description: Browser/server trust boundaries, HTTP, cookies, sessions, origins and attack surfaces.
learningObjectives: Test normal and malicious/invalid cases safely.

notes.text: Browser/server trust boundaries, HTTP, cookies, sessions, origins and attack surfaces.

Learn web security foundations by first identifying the asset and trust boundary, then understanding the attack or failure mode, then applying a defense and finally testing that defense. The objective is defensive engineering, not memorizing isolated vulnerabilities.

Web Security Foundations is important because security failures often happen at boundaries between users, browsers, APIs, services, databases and deployment systems. Students should learn to prevent, detect and safely remediate these failures.

notes.alt: Web Security Web Security Foundations security diagram
notes.caption: Add a defensive architecture diagram showing the trust boundary, threat and mitigation for Web Security Foundations.

items: Identify the asset being protected.
Identify the trust boundary and attacker capability.
Understand the failure/vulnerability mechanism.
Apply layered defensive controls.
Create a test that proves the control works.

notes.code:
Scenario: Map the attack surface of a modern web application.

Defensive workflow: identify the asset -> map the trust boundary -> define allowed behavior -> implement controls -> test negative cases -> monitor.

items: Locate the untrusted input or risky boundary.
Define what the application should allow.
Apply validation, authorization or isolation.
Verify the result with positive and negative tests.
Log the security-relevant event without exposing secrets.
Relying on client-side checks for security.
Using authentication without object-level authorization.
Logging passwords, tokens or sensitive personal data.
Fixing a symptom without identifying the trust boundary.
Skipping regression tests after a security fix.
Use defense in depth.
Enforce authorization on the server.
Keep secrets out of source code.
Prefer safe APIs and parameterized operations.
Automate security checks where practical.
Treat security findings as engineering work with owners and verification.
I can explain Web Security Foundations in my own words.
I can identify the affected trust boundary.
I can describe the defensive control.
I can create a negative test.
I can explain how the fix should be monitored.

modules.title: Web Security Testing
modules.description: Manual testing, automated scanning, secure test cases and vulnerability triage.

lessons.title: Web Security Testing
lessons.description: Manual testing, automated scanning, secure test cases and vulnerability triage.
learningObjectives: Test normal and malicious/invalid cases safely.

notes.text: Manual testing, automated scanning, secure test cases and vulnerability triage.

Learn web security testing by first identifying the asset and trust boundary, then understanding the attack or failure mode, then applying a defense and finally testing that defense. The objective is defensive engineering, not memorizing isolated vulnerabilities.

Web Security Testing is important because security failures often happen at boundaries between users, browsers, APIs, services, databases and deployment systems. Students should learn to prevent, detect and safely remediate these failures.

notes.caption: Add a defensive architecture diagram showing the trust boundary, threat and mitigation for Web Security Testing.

items: Identify the asset being protected.
Identify the trust boundary and attacker capability.
Understand the failure/vulnerability mechanism.
Apply layered defensive controls.
Create a test that proves the control works.

notes.code:
Scenario: Create a repeatable web-security test plan.

Defensive workflow: identify the asset -> map the trust boundary -> define allowed behavior -> implement controls -> test negative cases -> monitor.

items: Locate the untrusted input or risky boundary.
Define what the application should allow.
Apply validation, authorization or isolation.
Verify the result with positive and negative tests.
Log the security-relevant event without exposing secrets.
Relying on client-side checks for security.
Using authentication without object-level authorization.
Logging passwords, tokens or sensitive personal data.
Fixing a symptom without identifying the trust boundary.
Skipping regression tests after a security fix.
Use defense in depth.
Enforce authorization on the server.
Keep secrets out of source code.
Prefer safe APIs and parameterized operations.
Automate security checks where practical.
Treat security findings as engineering work with owners and verification.
I can explain Web Security Testing in my own words.
I can identify the affected trust boundary.
I can describe the defensive control.
I can create a negative test.
I can explain how the fix should be monitored.
